  "hypothesis": "Predicted that line patterns with salient Gestalt information would be processed as holistically as faces without any training, evidenced by a composite-face effect.",
  "design": "within-subject; factors were Task (faces vs. line patterns), Alignment (aligned vs. misaligned), Congruency (congruent vs. incongruent), and Same/Different (same vs. different top parts).",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Task type (composite-face task versus composite-pattern task using line patterns with salient Gestalt information), stimulus alignment, and flanker congruency.",
  "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d') in a same/different judgment task regarding the top parts of composite stimuli.",
  "population_and_setting": "Twenty-two participants from the University of Tübingen community tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 22,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Allowed 22 people to register in case some might not show up, and stopped data collection after testing all those who did show up.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (alignment) x 2 (congruency) x 2 (task) repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by separate ANOVAs and t-tests for each task.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks in random order with an intertrial interval of 1 second, completing eight practice trials before experimental trials."
